title: Every Markdown file in the projects
prompt:
Mira wants a list of all the documentation in her projects. Find every file whose name ends in `.md` anywhere below `~/projects`, and save the list, one path per line, into `markdown.txt` in her home directory.

Relative paths (`projects/…`) and absolute paths (`/home/mira/projects/…`) are both fine.
hints: `find` searches a directory and everything below it.
`-name` matches file names with a glob. Quote the pattern, so the shell doesn’t expand it first.
`find projects -name '*.md'` prints the paths; add `> markdown.txt`.
check:
if [ ! -e markdown.txt ]; then no "There is no markdown.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "markdown.txt exists."
norm() { sed -e 's#^/home/mira/##' -e 's#^~/##' -e 's#^\./##' "$@" | sort; }
if [ "$(norm markdown.txt)" = "$(find projects -name '*.md' | norm)" ]; then ok "It lists all four Markdown files, and nothing else."
else
  missing=$(comm -13 <(norm markdown.txt) <(find projects -name '*.md' | norm) | wc -l)
  extra=$(comm -23 <(norm markdown.txt) <(find projects -name '*.md' | norm) | wc -l)
  no "$missing Markdown file(s) are missing from the list, and $extra line(s) aren’t Markdown files below projects."
fi

title: A hidden backup
prompt:
Before Mira edits the studio website, she wants a copy of its start page out of sight.

Create a hidden directory named `.backup` inside `~/projects/website`, and copy `index.html` from `~/projects/website` into it. Then compare what `ls` and `ls -a` show in `~/projects/website`.
hints: A file or directory is hidden when its name starts with a dot.
`mkdir` creates the directory and `cp` copies the file.
`cp projects/website/index.html projects/website/.backup/` copies the file into the directory.
check:
d=projects/website/.backup
if [ -d $d ]; then ok "The hidden directory ~/$d exists."; else no "There is no directory ~/$d yet."; exit 1; fi
if cmp -s $d/index.html projects/website/index.html; then ok "It holds a copy of index.html."
else no "There is no copy of index.html in ~/$d."; fi
if [ -f projects/website/index.html ]; then ok "The original index.html is still in place."; else no "The original index.html is gone: copy it, don’t move it."; fi
